Setup environment

Download and organize the public data used in this analysis

Load published data from GSE152048

If not already done, download the data sets from the GEO repository, extract matrices, import into a Seurat object, perform initial QC and append relevant clinical data for each sample, as reported in the manuscript.

Code
# Make a list of sample names
geo1 <- tibble(
  name = c("X00003", "X00004", "X00005", "X00006", "X00007", "X00008",
    "X00010", "X00009", "X00011"),
  model = c("BC5", "BC6", "BC10", "BC11", "BC16",
    "BC17", "BC20", "BC21", "BC22"),
  qc = c(18000, 25000, 25000, 30000, 70000,
    40000, 70000, 50000, 50000),
  path = c("Conventional", "Conventional", "Conventional",
    "Conventional", "Conventional", "Chondroblastic",
    "Chondroblastic", "Intraosseous", "Chondroblastic"),
  type = c("Primary", "Primary", "Lung Met", "Primary", "Primary",
          "Lung Met", "Primary", "Primary", "Primary")
)

# Check if primary tumor directory exists and create if it doesn't
if(!dir.exists("public")) {
  tar_dir <- "public"
  dir.create(tar_dir)
}

# Download, extract, and organize the files from GEO
if(!dir.exists("public/GSE152048")) {
  tar_dir <- "public/GSE152048"
  dir.create(tar_dir)
  geo_pre <- "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE152nnn/GSE152048/suppl/GSE152048_"
  for(s in geo1$model){
    gse_path <- paste0(geo_pre, s, ".matrix.tar.gz")
    tar_file <- paste0(tar_dir, "/", s, ".tar.gz ")
    download.file(gse_path, destfile = tar_file, method = "auto")
    untar(tar_file, exdir = tar_dir)
    file.remove(tar_file)
  }
}

# Create a vector of normalized Seurat objects for all GSE152048 samples
human_geo <- future_lapply(geo1$model, function(s) {
  raw <- tenx_load_qc(paste0("public/GSE152048/",
                          s, "/"))
  raw <- subset(raw, subset = nCount_RNA < geo1$qc[geo1$model == s] & percent.mt <13)
  raw$src <- s
  raw$name <- geo1$name[geo1$model == s]
  raw$type <- geo1$type[geo1$model == s]
  raw$path <- geo1$path[geo1$model == s]
  raw$gse <- "GSE152048"
  raw <- raw %>%
    NormalizeData()
  return(raw)
})

human_geo <- merge(human_geo[[1]], human_geo[2:length(human_geo)],
    add.cell.ids = geo1$name) %>%
    JoinLayers()

qs::qsave(human_geo, "output/seurat_objects/human_geo.qs")

Co-culture experiments and NicheNET analysis

This script is organized generally into a series of subscripts that will process the raw data to generate figure panels as they are organized in the manuscript. The first of these will pull data from cell culture data–tumor cells and lung epithelial cells cultured either alone or together. This data will facilitate a ligand-receptor-target analysis designed to identify the mediators of the host-to-tumor interaction.

NicheNET analysis

Starting with tumor (OS-17) and lung (HBEC) cells cultured either as monocultures or co-cultures, leverage the NicheNET algorithm to ask the question:

What ligands produced by epithelial cells would bind receptors in osteosarcoma cells to cause the target gene changes that are observed in the co-culture?

Load and organize the co-culture data

Code
# scrna_path <- "../../../Counts_2/"
scrna_path <- "C:/Users/rxr014/OneDrive - Nationwide Children's Hospital/BIScratch/"

deets_cocx <- tribble(
    ~id, ~max_count, ~max_percent_mt, ~file,
    "S0001", 16000, 14, "S0001",
    "S0005", 16000, 14, "S0005")

cocx <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(deets_cocx)), function(i) {
    test <- tenx_load_qc(paste0(scrna_path,
                        deets_cocx$file[i],
                        "/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/"),
                 violin_plot = FALSE) %>%
        subset(nCount_RNA < deets_cocx$max_count[i] &
                   percent.mt < deets_cocx$max_percent_mt[i]) %>%
        process_seurat()
})

names(cocx) <- deets_cocx$id
for (i in seq_along(cocx)) {
    cocx[[i]]$src <- deets_cocx$id[i]
}

Intercellular signaling analysis on co-culture data

Which signals produced by lung epithelial cells elicit the transcriptional changes that we see in osteosarcoma cells in co-culture? In NicheNET, define the target gene set by DEG analysis comparing osteosarcoma cells in co-culture to cultured alone. Define senders as the epithelial cells and receivers as the osteosarcoma cells.

Code
cx <- merge(
    cocx$S0001,
    y = cocx$S0005,
    add.cell.ids = c("monocx", "cocx"),
    project = "InterSignaling") %>%
    JoinLayers()

cx <- process_seurat(cx, resolution  = 0.4)

p1 <- r_dim_plot(cx,
    group.by = "src",
    title = "Source")
p2 <- r_dim_plot(cx, "Clusters")
p3 <- r_feature_plot(cx, features = "KRT19", title = "KRT19")
p4 <- r_feature_plot(cx, features = "COL1A1", title = "COL1A1")

p <- p1 | p2 | p3 | p4
p

Code

Evaluate intratumoral heterogeneity in relation to paracrine signals

This script assesses patterns of gene expression within tumor cell subpopulations isolated from PDX models and human patients.

Heterogeneity analysis

Isolate the co-culture tumor and evaluate IL6 and CXCL8 expression

Code
# Load the processed culture data
cx <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/cx.qs")
tumor_cocx <- subset(cx, idents = "OS-CoCx")

# Remove the doublets that express epithelial markers
tumor_cocx <- subset(tumor_cocx, cells = readRDS("misc/doublets.rds"), invert = T)

tumor_cocx <- tumor_cocx %>%
    FindVariableFeatures() %>%
    RunPCA() %>%
    RunUMAP(
        dims = 1:20,
        n.neighbors = 20,
        min.dist = 0.1,
        local.connectivity = 5,
        spread = 1,
        verbose = FALSE) %>%
    FindNeighbors(verbose = FALSE) %>%
    FindClusters(verbose = FALSE, resolution = 0.25)

p1 <- r_dim_plot(tumor_cocx,
    title = "Tumor in Co-culture")
p2 <- DimPlot(tumor_cocx,
        cells.highlight = WhichCells(tumor_cocx, expression = IL6 > 3),
        cols.highlight = "#1F00B8",
        pt.size = 1) +
    labs(title = "IL6 Expression >3") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    coord_fixed()
p3 <- DimPlot(tumor_cocx,
        cells.highlight = WhichCells(tumor_cocx, expression = CXCL8 > 6),
        cols.highlight = "#1F00B8",
        pt.size = 1) +
    labs(title = "CXCL8 Expression >6") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    coord_fixed()
p4 <- r_feature_plot(tumor_cocx,
    "nCount_RNA",
    title = "Total Counts",
    max.cutoff = 12000)

p <- p1 | p2 | p3 | p4
p

Code
stash_plot(p, "Hetero-1")

qs::qsave(tumor_cocx, "output/seurat_objects/tumor_cocx.qs")
rm(tumor_cocx)

Intratumoral Heterogeneity - PDX Primary

Code
samples <- tribble(
  ~id, ~model, ~mt_cutoff, ~count_cutoff, ~species,
  "S0037", "OS-17", 25, 160000, "^GRCh38-"
)

s <- 1
pdx_tibia <- tenx_load_qc(
    paste0(pre_path, samples$id[s], post_path),
    species_pattern = samples$species[s],
    violin_plot = FALSE
  ) %>%
  subset(
    percent.mt < samples$mt_cutoff[s] &
    nCount_RNA < samples$count_cutoff[s]
  ) %>%
  NormalizeData()
pdx_tibia$id <- samples$id[s]
pdx_tibia$model <- samples$model[s]

pdx_tibia <- pdx_tibia %>%
  FindVariableFeatures(nfeatures = 5000) %>%
  ScaleData() %>%
  RunPCA()

pdx_tibia <- pdx_tibia %>%
  FindNeighbors(reduction = "pca", k.param = 200L) %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = 0.8) %>%
  RunUMAP(reduction = "pca", dims = 1:30)

Code
# Load tumor cells from the pre-processed patient data
# https://doi.org/10.1158/1078-0432.ccr-24-0049
pt_mets_1 <- qs::qread("public/integrated_lungs.qs") %>%
  subset(subset = met_labels == "Tumor") %>%
  subset(subset = method == "cell")

# And from the GEO dataset downloaded in download.qmd
pt_mets_2 <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/human_geo.qs") %>%
  subset(subset = type == "Lung Met") %>%
  subset(cells = tumor_cells)

# Align key metadata
pt_mets_2$id <- pt_mets_2$src
pt_mets_2$src <- "Geo"
pt_mets_2$method <- "cell"

# Merge and downsample
pt_mets_tumor <- merge(pt_mets_1, pt_mets_2) %>%
  JoinLayers() %>%
  subset(downsample = 1200) %>%
  ScaleData() %>%
  FindVariableFeatures(nfeatures = 5000) %>%
  RunPCA()

pt_mets_tumor <- pt_mets_tumor %>%
  harmony::RunHarmony(c("id"),
    dims.use = 1:50,
    theta = 8,
    sigma = .1,
    lambda = .3) %>%
  RunUMAP(dims = 1:50, reduction = "harmony") %>%
  FindNeighbors(reduction = "harmony") %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = 0.4) %>%
  run_fdl()

Brute force optimization of harmony parameters:

Ever find yourself banging your head against the wall trying to find the right combination of parameters that will make your samples magically meld into a beautiful orchestra of colorful dots? ::: {.cell hash=‘OS-lung_signaling_cache/html/load_sobjs_3f73393f530eece9c5a310ad42e9e6ed’}

Code
pdx_tibia <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/pdx_tibia.qs")
pdx_lungs <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/pdx_lungs.qs")
primaries <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/primaries.qs")
pt_mets_tumor <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/pt_mets_tumor.qs")

:::

Here’s a solution that finally worked for me…just test all the possible combinations: ::: {.cell hash=‘OS-lung_signaling_cache/html/brute_force_optimization_0e6d6209ec466bd5b447f04a8c697e78’}

Code
hopts <- tibble(
  theta = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8),
  sigma = c(.01, .03, .1, .3, 1),
  lambda = c(.1, .3, 1, 3, 10)
)
hopts <- expand.grid(hopts$theta, hopts$sigma, hopts$lambda) %>%
  setNames(colnames(hopts))
results <- parallel::mclapply(1:nrow(hopts), function(i) {
  sobj <- pt_mets_tumor %>%
    harmony::RunHarmony("id",
      dims.use = 1:50,
      theta = hopts$theta[i],
      sigma = hopts$sigma[i],
      lambda = hopts$lambda[i]) %>%
    RunUMAP(dims = 1:50, reduction = "harmony") %>%
    FindNeighbors(reduction = "harmony") %>%
    FindClusters(resolution = 0.4)
  return(
    r_dim_plot(sobj, 
      group.by = "id",
      order = TRUE,
      ) +
      ggtitle(paste0(
        "Theta ",
        hopts$theta[i],
        ", Sigma ",
        hopts$sigma[i],
        ", Lambda ",
        hopts$lambda[i]
      ))
  )
}, mc.cores = parallelly::availableCores())
format(object.size(results), "Gb")
patchwork::wrap_plots(results[1:25], ncol = 5)
patchwork::wrap_plots(results[26:50], ncol = 5)
patchwork::wrap_plots(results[51:75], ncol = 5)
patchwork::wrap_plots(results[76:100], ncol = 5)
patchwork::wrap_plots(results[101:125], ncol = 5)

:::

IL1-related activity within tumor cells

Here, we evaluate the same transcriptional data for evidence of IL1-driven tumor cell activation, as evidenced by signatures of NF-kB signaling.

Evaluate pathways downstream of IL1 (NF-kB)

Evaluate cell cycle and NF-kB - PDX Tibia

Code
# Load the dataset
pdx_tibia <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/pdx_tibia.qs")

# Determine cell cycle phase for each cell and plot
pdx_tibia <- kill_cc(pdx_tibia)

Code
# Pull the transcription-factor regulated gene sets from msigdb
sigs <- msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",
    category = "H") %>%
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol)

gs <- "HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB"

# Quantify the NF-kB pathway activity and plot
cell_ranks <- AUCell::AUCell_run(
  pdx_tibia[["RNA"]]$counts,
  sigs %>% filter(gs_name == gs) %>% pull(gene_symbol)
)
pdx_tibia$nfkb_activity <- AUCell::getAUC(cell_ranks)[1,]

# Set scale common to IL1R1 plots
nfkb_scale <- scale_color_gradient(
  limits = c(0.1, 0.35), 
  # colors = c("#EEEEEE", "#AE0600"),
  low = "#EEEEEE",
  high = "#AE0600",
  oob = scales::squish
  )

p1 <- FeaturePlot(pdx_tibia,
  "nfkb_activity",
  reduction = "fdl",
  pt.size = 1,
  order = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed() +
  nfkb_scale
p1

Evaluate cell cycle and NF-kB - PDX Lung Mets

Code
# Load the dataset
pdx_lungs <- qs::qread("output/seurat_objects/pdx_lungs.qs")

# Determine cell cycle phase for each cell and plot

[1] "No CC regression performed."
Code
p6 <- r_dim_plot(pdx_lungs,
    reduction = "fdl",
    group.by = "Phase",
    label = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "OS-17 Lung Mets - Cell Cycle") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
p6

Code
# Quantify the NF-kB pathway activity and plot
cell_ranks <- AUCell::AUCell_run(
  pdx_lungs[["RNA"]]$counts,
  sigs %>% filter(gs_name == gs) %>% pull(gene_symbol)
)
pdx_lungs$nfkb_activity <- AUCell::getAUC(cell_ranks)[1,]

p2 <- FeaturePlot(pdx_lungs,
  "nfkb_activity",
  reduction = "fdl",
  pt.size = 1,
  order = TRUE) +
  coord_fixed() +
  nfkb_scale
p2
